what: Why the mode-2 brink check cut flicker on lab_voidcorner and not on dm4, read from the listen tapes of its two rungs (runs/lab-voidcorner-brink-flicker.results.json and its -dm4 twin hold every tape's map and SHA-256). No new matches.

signature.method: routed deflection episodes led into by route steering and followed by four route frames: share whose wish turned more than two degrees towards the velocity heading of the hazard run (the guard's held heading) over three frames
signature.reading: the check acted on both maps; it opened on dm4, less often

re_entry_kinds.method: a re-entry is a routed episode after at most two route frames since the previous one; at its last route frame the wish heading and the velocity heading are probed 48u ahead at origin height with a hull-0 column scan of the map's BSP: lava or slime above the first solid, or no solid within 280u, is a hazard (the guard's floor rules without its speed-dependent run-off landing test)

reading: Where the wanted heading itself points at lava or a void the check works alike on both maps: those re-entries fell 37 per cent on the lab map and 41 per cent on dm4. They are 95 per cent of re-entries on the lab map, every lip of which is lethal, and 39 per cent on dm4, most of whose re-entries happen where neither the wish nor the velocity sees lava or a void within the guard's floor reach, which points at the speed-dependent run-off landing test (not measured). The lab map over-represented the one lip type the check can act on.
